issues.description: The proposal commits to a 'fixed-fee structure capped strictly at $300,000'. The Client Matrix explicitly marks the budget cap as a 'contradicted' item (Rita insists on a $300k cap, while Sarah expects a $250k to $400k range). Stating a contradicted item as a firm fact rather than placing it in Open Questions violates the matrix instructions and risks alienating stakeholders.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the strict $300,000 cap from the Pricing Approach. Present a proposed fixed-fee structure or range, and add a specific item to the Open Questions section to resolve the budget cap discrepancy between stakeholders.

issues.description: The proposal fails to address the fundamental, 'contradicted' disagreement regarding whether to invest in a short-term workflow fix or a long-term platform replacement. While the proposal attempts to bridge this with a 'portable architecture', it completely omits this major stakeholder misalignment from the Open Questions section.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a new item to the Open Questions section explicitly addressing the strategic disagreement between replacing Routemaster with a SaaS platform versus incrementally fixing existing workflows. Frame the proposed 'portable logic layer' as a potential compromise to be validated during kickoff.

risks: Committing to a strict $300k budget cap before resolving the internal client disagreement could force the consulting team to absorb costs if the scope aligns closer to the $400k expectations of other stakeholders.

Proceeding with an incremental workflow fix without explicitly acknowledging and resolving Marcus's desire for a full platform replacement risks poor adoption and lack of technical buy-in during execution.
